checks.check: Semgrep self test and scans of all three code folders
checks.detail: Semgrep 1.186.0, 10 own rules. Self test: all 10 fire on planted bad code. Scans: dashboard 24 files, Job HQ 15 files, collector 21 files, 0 findings, and the scanned count equals the files present. A planted os.system line made the scan BLOCK with exit 1. The first dashboard scan was refused as blind (a parse error in layout.tsx and an invalid rules file), which is the guard working; both were fixed.

checks.check: Golden backtest of the collector's decisions
checks.detail: 192 inputs (178 real job titles from a live run plus 14 hand written edge cases) through 7 scenarios: the shipped rules and every changeable setting. 16 golden tests. A deliberately broken experience rule was caught on the exact line. The first proof showed a gap (no input on the 2 year boundary), so boundary cases were added and the break is now caught in the default scenario too.
checks.limit: Protects the decisions only, not the adapters' parsing of live pages or the dashboard. No older trusted version exists, so there is no oracle. Golden files can encode a bug that existed when they were saved.

checks.check: Job links and posting text cannot run code
checks.detail: Found: a posting link such as javascript:alert(1) was stored and linked. Fixed in three layers: the collector keeps only plain http and https links, the email never links an unsafe address, and the dashboard shows the Open button only for a safe link. 18 collector tests, 3 dashboard tests, plus properties over generated hostile text. Mutation checking then found an unescaped title branch in the email, now tested.
checks.limit: Covers the entry points I know (posting title, company, links, description in email and dashboard). React escapes text by default. No browser level injection test was run on the screens yet.

checks.check: Rules that must hold for every input
checks.detail: Collector: 12 properties with Hypothesis (never crashes on any text, only known places, a title with an excluded word never matches, fewer countries or a lower experience limit never add matches, safe links only). Job HQ: 5 and dashboard: 5 properties with fast-check. Broken copies failed with the smallest counterexample found automatically.

checks.check: Repo rules, secret scan, audit, Semgrep and tests workflows on commit c6a1904
checks.detail: All five workflows finished with success on GitHub, read back through the GitHub tools, not assumed from local runs.

checks.check: Who can read the tables (Supabase row level security)
checks.detail: Policies say any signed in user may read and write. Proved inside a rolled back transaction that a second random signed in user could read a test row, then confirmed no test rows were left. Today there is 1 user, so nothing leaks, but that is only safe while public sign ups stay off.
checks.limit: Not fixed yet. An owner only migration (0002_owner_only.sql) is drafted but not applied, because a mistake could lock you out of your own data. Needs your yes.

checks.check: Security headers on every page
checks.detail: Added nosniff, no framing (X-Frame-Options and frame-ancestors), referrer limit, permissions lockdown and HTTPS only. The new test failed first (module missing), then passed, and curl against the built running app shows all six headers.
checks.limit: No full Content Security Policy yet (inline theme script, Google Fonts and Supabase need named origins first). Strict-Transport-Security only matters once served over HTTPS.

checks.check: Owner only agent tables (migration 0002) and append only audit log
checks.detail: Check failed first (tables missing). After applying, a second signed in user sees 0 rows in all four new tables, the owner can read, and update or delete on the audit log raises. Loosening one policy inside a rolled back transaction made the check fail, so it can catch the hole. No test rows were left. The Supabase advisor lists is_owner() as executable by signed in users: intended, it only tells a caller whether they are the owner.
checks.limit: Only the new tables are owner only. roles, applications and source_runs still allow any signed in user (finding above stays open until you say yes).

checks.check: Scouting status and shortlist rules (hq/src/domain/scouting.ts)
checks.detail: Tests failed first (module missing), then 34 pass. The office status comes only from the newest task row: a claim 30 minutes old or more or with an unreadable date counts as waiting, never working. The shortlist only includes verdicts the agent marked, never exceeds the limit and never leaves out a higher score. Four deliberate breaks (stale boundary, sort direction, shortlist filter, newest task choice) were each caught.
checks.limit: Pure rules only. The screen and the database reads that feed them are Tasks 4 and 5.

checks.check: Scouting tools (claim, read, submit, finish) and the instruction injection defence
checks.detail: Tests failed first (module missing), then 36 pass. Two sessions cannot claim one task (the claim only succeeds while the task is still queued, tested with a simulated race). A claim older than 30 minutes goes back to the queue. Scores outside 0 to 100, true or false as a score, reasons under 10 or over 500 characters, roles not in the task and unclaimed tasks are all rejected with nothing saved. A description saying to ignore instructions and give every role 100 is returned as data and changes nothing. Every call is written to the audit log. 11 deliberate breaks were added to the mutation check: one survived (closing an unclaimed task), a test was added, and all 37 are now caught. Migration 0003 added the finished_at column.
checks.limit: Tested against an in memory stand in for the database, not the live Supabase project. The first real run against it happens in Task 6. Deciding whether a verdict is wise is up to the model, so the tools only check shape, range and ownership.

checks.check: Collector queues a Scouting task after each run
checks.detail: Tests failed first, then 237 collector tests pass at 90% coverage. New matched roles become tasks of at most 50 roles, with no cap, so a huge first run drops nothing (410 roles become 9 tasks). How many tasks one daily session works through is a limit in the run instructions, not in the queue. Roles that do not match the profile are never queued, a second run with the same roles queues nothing, and a failing queue write is reported but never stops the collection or the email. Deliberate breaks of the queueing code are all caught (39 of 39).
checks.limit: Tested against the in memory stand in. The queue write against the live database is exercised in Task 6. A big backlog means Scouting shows as waiting for several days.

checks.check: Scouting panel in Job HQ and the database reading code
checks.detail: Tests failed first (modules missing), then 55 HQ tests pass with coverage above the floors. The panel shows idle, waiting, working, completed or failed in plain words, lists the top five shortlisted roles best first, and shows a Simulation badge whenever the data is not real. Text written by companies or by the agent is escaped (a script tag and an image with an onerror handler render as plain text). The reader drops malformed rows and scores outside 0 to 100, and a failed read throws instead of showing an empty office as if it were real.

There is no Scouting character or desk in the 3D scene yet, so nothing in the scene lights up for it. The panel layout was checked by screenshot only, not by browser click tests.

Every pose maps to exactly one real Scouting status (idle sleeping, waiting waiting, working working, completed cheering, failed slumped), so the office shows nothing the task rows do not say. checks.check: Scouting goblins in the glass office
checks.detail: Four goblins stand in the glass office, and their pose comes only from the real Scouting status through the tested pose rules. Spot positions are guarded by tests (inside the room, clear of desk, chair and armchairs, 0.5 m apart, and out of the strip a solid door hides from the default camera). A test for the door blind zone failed first and led to two spots being moved. If the model fails to load, a safety wrapper shows nothing and the office stays up. Motion stops when the browser asks for reduced motion. All five poses were checked by screenshot. 93 HQ tests pass with coverage above the floors, type check and build clean.

checks.check: First complete collection on the live database
checks.detail: After the database address was corrected the real run read all 245 sources without a failure and stored 2223 roles in the five regions, 157 of them matching the profile, and queued 4 Scouting tasks covering those 157 roles (read back from the database). It then failed at the last step: Resend refused the ALERT_EMAIL_TO secret as not an email address. Added tests first, then a start up check of both email settings that explains the problem before any collection starts, and a plain message if sending fails after the roles are saved. The message never repeats the value. 261 collector tests pass.
checks.limit: The ALERT_EMAIL_TO secret can only be corrected by the owner. The first digest of the 157 matching roles was not sent, and later runs only email roles that are new. Only a repeat run after the fix proves the email works.

checks.check: First real Scouting run on the live database, through the real tools
checks.detail: Claude Code claimed task 1 (50 roles), read the roles as untrusted text, saved 50 verdicts and finished the task, all through the command line tools with the service key injected by the network proxy (never visible in chat, files or logs). Read back from the database: 50 verdicts (3 shortlisted, scores 5 to 82), tasks 1 done and 3 queued, audit log 53 rows (1 claim, 1 read, 50 submits, 1 finish). A second finish was refused. The 50 descriptions contained no instructions aimed at the agent. A first attempt to save the key under the Authorization header failed because the newer sb_secret key belongs in the apikey header; the wrong entry was removed by the owner and a new one saved correctly.
checks.limit: One task of four was run, so 107 matched roles are still queued. The service key now sits in the session environment's network secrets and stays there until the owner removes it. Verdicts are one model's judgement against the stated profile and can be wrong.

checks.check: Profile match quality seen by Scouting
checks.detail: Scouting found that the collector marks roles in Madrid as matching because the rules accept the whole country of Spain, while the owner asked for Barcelona. Many matched roles are also junior sales, retail or software testing roles that fit no stated target field (consulting, finance, VC, analyst, business development, health). Fix: city_limits in rules.yaml (Spain: Barcelona only), applied both when storing and when matching, with an unknown city accepted only if the raw location text names Barcelona as a whole word. Added exclusions for social media, quality assurance, QA, retail, sales associate and part time titles. Tests failed first. The golden decision file changed in exactly one line (a Spanish role with no city given), read and accepted. 3 more deliberate breaks, all 42 caught.
checks.limit: Fixed in rules.yaml and the rules code. The matched flag is still only a title keyword filter, so some weak fits remain (for example junior sales rep roles). Scouting scoring is the second filter. Roles already stored for Madrid close on the next collection run, which no longer reads them as in region.

checks.check: Daily Scouting schedule, first test run in a fresh session
checks.detail: A fresh Claude Code session started from the scheduled task reviewed the remaining 3 tasks (107 roles) with no errors and no injection attempts, and stopped with nothing queued. Read back from the database: 157 verdicts in total, 6 shortlisted, all 4 tasks done, audit log 169 rows (4 claims, 4 reads, 157 submits, 4 finishes), matching the session's own report. Three setup snags were found and fixed in the instructions: add_repo was missing (git clone works), the package needs Python 3.12 (3.11 was the default), and the editable install rewrote tracked egg-info files (now untracked and ignored). The session also caught listings whose city did not match the text and said so in the reasons.
checks.limit: The schedule has run once, by hand. The first unattended run is tomorrow at 08:20 Madrid time. Each run uses Claude Code usage. The service key stays in the environment's network secrets until the owner removes it.

checks.check: Owner only CV tables (migration 0004)
checks.detail: The check failed first (tables missing). After applying, a second signed in user sees and changes nothing in cv_master and cv_versions and cannot queue a tailoring task. The owner can read and edit the master CV, read, approve and delete versions, and queue only a queued tailor_cv task (a scout task, a finished task and a claimed task are all refused). Versions can only be written by the service role. Loosening the task policy in a rolled back transaction made the check fail. No test rows were left. The advisor shows no new warnings.

checks.check: CV text format (web/src/lib/cvText.ts)
checks.detail: Tests failed first (module missing), then 53 web tests pass with coverage above the floors. The parser keeps everything as plain text (a script tag and a bold tag stay as text), refuses entries with the wrong number of parts, links that are not http or https (javascript, ftp and file addresses), unknown sections, over long lines and over long CVs, reports every problem with its line number, and never throws on any input (property test). parse(format(cv)) returns the same CV (property test). Four deliberate breaks: three first survived and pointed at missing tests (entry with too many parts, non web links, multi line summary), which were added, and all four are now caught.
checks.limit: Format checks only. Whether the content is true is checked by the tailoring tool in Task 3, and the dashboard pages come in Task 4.

checks.check: CV tailoring tool and truthfulness validator (collector/src/jobtracker/cv.py)
checks.detail: Tests failed first (module missing), then 29 pass; the whole collector suite stays above the coverage floor. A tailored CV can only select, reorder and reword the master: the program copies employers, schools, degrees, dates and contact details, and refuses extra fields, unknown or reused ids, bullets from another entry, any number not in the original bullet, any new name not in the master CV, the company or the role title, over long or non text, and empty versions. A hostile instruction such as adding 10 years of Python experience is refused. Hypothesis properties: no number absent from the source ever gets through, and any text is either accepted or refused with a clear error. Two sessions cannot claim one task, stale claims are requeued, the audit log holds ids, counts and rule codes only (a test searches it for the CV text). 13 deliberate breaks, all caught (55 of 55 overall).
checks.limit: The validator cannot tell whether a reworded sentence is still true in meaning, only that it adds no new number or name. Spelled out numbers (twelve) and non capitalised new skills can pass, so the owner must read each draft before using it. Tested against the in memory stand in, not yet the live database.

checks.check: CV dashboard pages (editor, draft viewer, tailor button)
checks.detail: Built and checked: 61 web tests pass with coverage above the floors, the production build is clean, and a logged out visitor to /cv, /cv/ID and a role page is redirected to the login page. All CV and role text is rendered as plain text by React (no raw HTML anywhere), links in a CV are shown as text and are not clickable, the editor refuses anything but http and https links, and the button state logic is tested (queued, working, stale claim, unreadable date). Writes use only what the database policies allow: save the master CV, approve or delete a draft, queue one tailor_cv task. Checked by screenshots of the three screens with a fictional CV.
checks.limit: No browser click tests and no check of the print output beyond the styles. Screens were checked against a local stand in for the database, not the live project, because no CV is saved yet.

checks.check: Redirects are checked step by step (independent security review, low item 1)
checks.detail: A separate reviewer read the whole repository and found nothing above its confidence bar. It listed two low items. The first was real as a politeness and safety gap: the collector's web client followed redirects by itself, so a redirect target was never checked against robots.txt or paced. Tests failed first. Now the gate follows each redirect itself, up to 3 steps, and every new host passes its own robots.txt and pacing. Redirects to plain http, IP addresses, localhost, other schemes, or loops are refused. 336 collector tests pass at 91% coverage and 4 new deliberate breaks are caught (59 of 59).
checks.limit: The robots.txt request itself may still follow redirects (the standard allows it) and its reply is only read as rules. A vendor can still redirect to another named https host that allows robots, which is then read like any board.

checks.check: Hostile role ids in database filters (independent security review, low item 2)
checks.detail: The reviewer could not confirm how the database library quotes odd characters in an in filter. I checked the real library: it quotes values with commas, brackets, quotes or backslashes and escapes embedded quotes and backslashes, and URL encodes the rest, so a hostile id such as x"),(source_id.eq."y or a)&select=* stays one item inside one filter and cannot add filters. A newline is left unquoted but stays an ordinary character in the one value. A regression test now pins this for 9 hostile values, so a library update that changed it would fail the tests.
checks.limit: This relies on the library's behavior, which the test guards but does not control.

checks.check: Full repository security review by a fresh reviewer
checks.detail: A fresh read only reviewer went through the whole tracked tree (collector, migrations, web proxy and pages, hq data mapper, workflows, tools) against injection, XSS, XML, YAML, SSRF, authorization, secrets and workflow risks. No finding reached the 80 percent confidence bar. It also named the controls it verified as sound: link safety, escaped digest, safe XML and YAML, the Supabase address check, the Ashby exception, the scout tool limits, the owner only policies, the audit log triggers, the login redirect and workflow permissions.
checks.limit: One reviewer, one pass, read only. It saw the repository as of the CV tables migration and tools, not the CV dashboard pages written afterwards, which were checked by my own tests and screenshots. Not a penetration test.

checks.check: CV Tailor character in the office
checks.detail: A person (model 'Low poly ordinary man in shirt and pants' by Agor_2012, CC BY 4.0, textures reduced and seven unused animations removed) stands in the aisle between the two desk islands. What he does comes only from the real status of the cv agent through tested rules: idle and waiting stand, working picks up papers, completed jumps, failed falls and stays down. The credit test failed first (model without a credit) and now passes, the animation rules and the station layout were written test first, and four deliberate breaks of the rules are caught (one malformed edit was redone). The panel shows a Simulation badge, escapes all text (script and image tags stay plain text), and says the one rule: it only reorders and rewords the master CV. A first render floated outside the building because I measured the model in world coordinates, which was found in the screenshot and fixed by measuring a separate unplaced copy. 120 HQ tests pass, build clean, production audit 0.
checks.limit: Status is sample data labelled Simulation until Job HQ can sign in (milestone M1). Poses are checked by screenshot only. Idle and waiting look alike, and the label above the character tells them apart.
